topics.title: Famous Temples in India
topics.description: Brihadeeswarar, Sun Temple Konark, Meenakshi, Kedarnath, Somnath, architecture and dynasties.

rows: The temple on Tirumala hills is also known as Tirupathi Balaji temple. It is also called a temple of seven hills. The temple is in Dravidian Architecture style.

It is a Buddhist temple. The Central Tower Of Mahabodhi is 180 feet tall i.e. 54 metres. It is one of the oldest brick structures. The brickwork depicts the life of Buddha. It is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.

It is lso known as Deo Patan. It is one of the 12 jyotirlinga shrines of Lord Shiva. There is no land in between seashores from Somnath temple to Antarctica. Constructed in Chalukyan style. 1947 - Sardar Vallabh Bhai Patel ordered the reconstruction of the temple that completed in 1951.
It is also known as Jagat Mandir. It is one of the four Hindu pilgrimages (Char Dham). The original structure was destroyed by Mahmud Brgada in 1472. Presently, in the Chalukya architecture style.
It is 5200 feet above sea level atop Trikuta Hills. It is a Cave temple.
A cave temple situated at an altitude of 3888 metres. It is one of the 51 Shakti Peeths. It is believed that Bhrigu Muni (A great sage) was the first to have discovered Amarnath.
Built by Lakkana Dandesha, a chieftain under the ruler Deva Raya II of the Vijayanagara Empire. It forms a part of Group of Monuments at Hampi that is designated as UNESCO World Heritage Site.

It is also known as Bahubali temple. The tallest monolithic statue (Of Gomateshwara) in the world carved out of a single block of granite. It is a Jain temple that is 57 feet high. Bahubali statue is one of the largest free-standing statues in the world depicting the prolonged meditation of Bahubali.
The architecture is the fusion of Chera and Dravidian styles.

They are a group of temples built by the rulers of Chandela Dynasty. There were 85 temples scattered over an area of 9 square miles, of which only 25 temples are remaining. Famous for nagara style architecture and known for extensive erotic sculptures.
It is one of the richest temples in India. It was constructed by Laxman Vithu & Dubai Patil in 1801.

Build in the 13th century by King Narasimhadeva I (AD 1238-1264) during the Ganga Empire. It is conceived as a gigantic chariot of the Sun God built in Kalinga architecture (Odisha style of architecture).

It is also called Yamanika Tirtha. This temple in Puri is famous for its annual chariot festival, Ratha Yatra. The first Jagannath temple was commissioned by King Indradyumna. Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra are a trio of deities worshipped at the temple.
It is a gurudwara, built in the 15th century. It is also known as Harmindar Sahib. Temple was plated in Gold in 1980 from the wealth and material donated by Maharaja Ranjit Singh.

One of the twelve Jyotirlinga temples built in the 12th Century. It has the longest corridor among all Hindu temples in India. It is built in the Dravidian style of architecture. Creators - Pandyas and Jaffna Kings There are 64 Tīrthas i.e. holy water bodies in and around the island of Rameswaram. It is also one of the Char Dhams.

It has Dravidian Architecture and over 40 inscriptions. There are 985 richly carved pillars that depict scenes from the wedding of Meenakshi (Parvati) and Sundareswarar (Shiva). It is famous for its 3 storied Gopuram at the main entrance.

One of the most important of 108 (Divya Desam )Vishnu Temples. It is built in Dravidian style, constructed in Vijayanagar Period. It is located on the island formed by twin river- Cauvery & Coleroon. 1st temple to be awarded by the UN Body for protecting and conserving cultural heritage. Its Gopuram is the biggest Gopuram in Asia. Also, it is the largest functioning Hindu temple in the world.

Also known as Raja Rajeswara Temple located at Thanjavur. This Dravidian style temple was built by the Chola emperor Raja Raja Chola I. One of the tallest temples in India that is completely made of Granite. It is one of the Great Living Chola Temples, along with Gangaikonda Cholapuram temple and Airavatesvara temple. It is also called Dakshin Meru and is situated on the bank of Cauvery river. It is a part of UNESCO World Heritage Sites.
It is created in Dravidian style, it is also called Dakshina Dwaraka. It has one of the largest temple tanks in India called Haridra Nadhi.

The temple wall carvings display all the 108 karanas from the Natya Shastra by Bharata Muni; these postures form the foundation of Bharatanatyam, a classical Indian dance. It was built in the 10th century when Chidambaram was the capital of the Chola dynasty. It is one of the oldest surviving active temple complexes in South India.

The original Vishwanath temple was destroyed by the army of Qutb-Uddin Aibak in 1194 CE when he defeated the Raja of Kannauj. There is a small well in the temple called the Jnana Vapi also spelt as Gyaan Vapi In 1669 CE, Emperor Aurangzeb destroyed the temple and built the Gyanvapi Mosque in its place. In 1780, Malhar Rao’s daughter-in-law Ahilyabai Holkar constructed the present temple adjacent to the mosque It is one of the 12 Jyotirlingas.

It is located in Garhwal hill along the banks of Alaknanda River. It is at an elevation of 3,133 metres i.e. 10,279 ft above the mean sea level. The temple is mentioned in ancient religious texts like Vishnu Purana and Skanda Purana.
Situated at an altitude of 3,291 metres i.e. 10,797 ft. It is located on the backdrop of Bandarpunch It is dedicated to goddess Yamuna.

topics.title: Classical Dances of India
topics.description: 8 Sangeet Natak Akademi classical dances: Bharatanatyam, Kathak, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, etc.

rows: What are the two basic aspects of Classical Dance?
There are two basic aspects of Natya Shastra: Lasya Tandava
It denotes grace, bhava, rasa and abhinaya. It is symbolic to the feminine features of dance as an art form
This is symbolic to the male aspects of dance and has more emphasis on rhythm and movement
What are the three basic elements of a classical dance act?

There are three basic elements: Nritta - These are the basic dance steps and are performed rhythmically but devoid of any expression or mood Natya - It means dramatic representations and refers to the story that is elaborated through the dance recital Nritya - refers to the sentiment and the emotions evoked through dance. It includes the mime and the different methods of expression including mudras in the dance
It forms the core of the Indian Classical Dance forms. The basic meaning is that each dance form is related to a Guru (Teacher) and he/she transfers that knowledge of dance to a Shishya (Student.)

phobias-list.question: What is the extreme or irrational fear of heights known as in medical science?

phobias-list.explanation: Hydrophobia (water aversion caused by throat spasms when swallowing liquids) is a classic manifestation of human rabies.

indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.question: Which premier civil service cadre is primarily responsible for staffing India's diplomatic missions and embassies abroad?

indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.question: What is an Indian diplomatic mission head called when appointed to a fellow Commonwealth country (e.g., United Kingdom, Canada, Australia)?
indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.hindiQuestion: राष्ट्रमंडल (Commonwealth) देशों (जैसे यूके, कनाडा, ऑस्ट्रेलिया) में तैनात भारतीय राजनयिक मिशन प्रमुख को क्या कहा जाता है?
indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.explanation: In Commonwealth countries, heads of missions are called High Commissioners (and missions are High Commissions); in non-Commonwealth countries they are called Ambassadors.
indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.hindiExplanation: राष्ट्रमंडल देशों में राजनयिक प्रमुख को 'उच्चायुक्त' (High Commissioner) और अन्य देशों में 'राजदूत' (Ambassador) कहा जाता है।

indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.question: Who was India's first Ambassador to the United States of America (1947-1948)?

indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.explanation: Prominent freedom fighter Asaf Ali was appointed independent India's first ambassador to the United States in 1947.

indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.question: Who was the first woman to serve as President of the United Nations General Assembly (in 1953) and an Indian Ambassador to the USSR and USA?

indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.question: What is the primary difference between an Embassy and a Consulate General?
indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.hindiQuestion: एक दूतावास (Embassy) और महावाणिज्य दूतावास (Consulate General) में मुख्य अंतर क्या है?
options: An Embassy is located in the host nation's capital handling political relations; Consulates are in regional commercial cities handling visas and trade
Consulates have military troops, embassies do not
Consulates are only for Commonwealth nations
hindiOptions: दूतावास मेजबान देश की राजधानी में मुख्य राजनीतिक संबंधों के लिए होता है; कांसुलेट अन्य वाणिज्यिक शहरों में वीजा व व्यापार के लिए होते हैं
दूतावास केवल वीजा जारी करता है
कांसुलेट केवल राष्ट्रमंडल के लिए हैं
indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.explanation: A country has one Embassy in the capital city (e.g. Washington D.C.), and multiple Consulates General in major business cities (e.g. New York, San Francisco, Chicago).

indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.question: Under which international convention is diplomatic immunity guaranteed to ambassadors and embassies worldwide?
indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.hindiQuestion: किस अंतरराष्ट्रीय सम्मेलन के तहत दुनिया भर के राजदूतों और दूतावासों को राजनयिक छूट (Diplomatic Immunity) प्राप्त है?
indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.explanation: The Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations (1961) codified the principles of diplomatic immunity, inviolability of embassy premises, and courier protections.
indian-ambassadors-to-foreign-countries-.hindiExplanation: 1961 का विएना कन्वेंशन राजनयिकों और दूतावासों को विशेष कानूनी सुरक्षा और छूट की गारंटी देता है।
